title: Project configuration
summary: A single, shareable project configuration replaces Jira's schemes: issue types and their hierarchy, system and custom fields with visible/required rules per type and workflow step, one workflow per issue type (statuses in three categories, table-based transitions with conditions, validators, post-functions and optional transition screens, read-only graph), creation/view/transition screens and notification rules. All labels are translatable JSONB with a fallback language. Changing a shared configuration shows the affected projects; a project can detach by duplicating; workflow or type changes open a mapping wizard that migrates tickets in the background. The workflow rule engine lives in `crates/domain` and is executed on tickets in L05; assigning a configuration to projects requires L03 nodes.

stories.title: Create a shareable project configuration and assign it
stories.i_want: to create a project configuration, assign it to several projects and see which projects share it
stories.so_that: projects that work the same way are configured once
acceptance: Given I am configuration admin, When I create configuration "Software development", Then it is created with default issue types, fields and a standard workflow
Given a configuration used by 6 projects, When I open it, Then a chip shows "Shared by 6 projects" and the Projects tab lists them
Given I edit a shared configuration, When I publish my changes, Then I first see the list of affected projects and must confirm
Given project PLAT uses a shared configuration, When I detach PLAT, Then its configuration is duplicated and further changes to the original no longer affect it
Given a tenant admin or configuration admin, When they manage configurations, Then it is allowed; Given any other user, Then the API answers 403

Unit tests cover draft change counting

Cross-tenant test proves configurations never leak

stories.title: Define issue types and their hierarchy
stories.i_want: to define issue types such as Epic, Story, Task, Sub-task, Bug with their parent-child hierarchy
stories.so_that: tickets are structured to match how each team breaks down work

Given types Epic > Story > Task > Sub-task, When I set Story's allowed parent to Epic, Then the hierarchy depth is defined by these rules
Given a hierarchy, When I try to make a type its own ancestor, Then it is refused
Given a type is used by tickets, When I remove it, Then publishing requires the mapping wizard to choose a replacement type
Given the identifier `bug` already exists in the configuration, When I add another `bug`, Then it is refused

Given the MVP field types (short text, rich long text, number, checkbox, date, date-time, single select, multi-select, cascading select, users, group, labels, URL, link to a ticket), When I create a field, Then each type is offered with its specific options

Given system fields such as Points and Remaining work, When I view the fields list, Then they are marked System and cannot be deleted
Given a list value used by tickets, When I remove it, Then it is deactivated rather than deleted so existing tickets keep their value

stories.so_that: each type of work follows its own lifecycle while reports stay consistent

Given every status, When I save, Then it belongs to exactly one category among To do, In progress and Done
Given statuses, When I add transition "Start" from To do to In progress, or from all statuses, Then it appears in the transitions table
Given the workflow, When I view it, Then a read-only graph shows statuses colored by category and transitions as labelled arrows
Given a workflow with no initial status or an unreachable status, When I publish, Then publishing is refused with an explicit error

stories.title: Configure transition conditions, validators and post-functions
stories.i_want: to restrict transitions to roles or groups, require fields, run post-functions and show a transition screen
stories.so_that: the workflow enforces our process rules automatically
acceptance: Given transition "Validate" restricted to role Reviewer, When a user without that role on the project requests it, Then it is not offered and the API refuses it
Given transition "Send to review" with validator "Remaining work required", When the field is empty, Then the transition is refused with the field named
Given transition "Start" with post-function "Assign to current user", When it runs, Then the ticket is assigned to the user
Given post-functions set or clear a field and add a comment, When the transition runs, Then they are applied in order in the same transaction
Given transition "Reject" with a transition screen asking for a rejection reason, When the user triggers it, Then the screen is shown before the transition

tech.title: Implement the transition rule engine in the domain
tech.description: Implement in `crates/domain` conditions (roles, groups), validators (required fields) and post-functions (assign, set field, clear field, add comment) as data-driven rules, with a pure function evaluating a transition request against a ticket snapshot and actor context and returning either errors or the list of changes to apply. Executed on tickets in L05.
done_when: Unit tests cover every condition, validator and post-function type and their combinations
Unit tests cover deterministic ordering of post-functions
Integration coverage through T02 endpoints and later L05 ticket transitions

stories.title: Migrate tickets with the status and type mapping wizard
stories.i_want: a wizard mapping removed statuses and types to new ones when I publish a workflow or configuration change
stories.so_that: existing tickets are migrated safely without losing their history
acceptance: Given workflow "Standard v2" removes "In test" and adds "In acceptance" for 6 projects, When I publish, Then the wizard lists each current status with its ticket count and a target status select
Given every removed status or type is mapped, When I confirm "Migrate 2,172 tickets", Then the migration runs in the background and I can follow its progress
Given the migration runs, When a ticket is migrated, Then its history records the old and new status with origin "system"
Given a status that is unmapped, When I try to confirm, Then the button stays disabled
Given the migration fails midway, When the job is retried, Then it resumes without migrating a ticket twice

tech.title: Compute required mappings and their ticket counts
